cheeger_target: There exists a numerical c>0 independent of dimension and measure such that every full-dimensional log-concave probability law mu with covariance Sigma has h_mu>=c/sqrt(||Sigma||_op). Here h_mu is the infimum of mu^+(A)/min(mu(A),1-mu(A)) over measurable A of mass strictly between zero and one, using outer Euclidean Minkowski boundary content mu^+(A)=liminf_(epsilon down to 0) [mu(A+epsilon B_2)-mu(A)]/epsilon. For isotropic laws, Sigma=I.
